bottom_line: In this trial comparing rivaroxaban with warfarin in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, the primary end point occurred at 1.7% per year vs. 2.2% per year (hazard ratio 0.79; 95% CI, 0.66 to 0.96; P<0.001 for noninferiority).
implications: These data support that rivaroxaban achieved noninferiority to warfarin for stroke or systemic embolism in the per-protocol, as-treated analysis (hazard ratio 0.79; 95% CI, 0.66 to 0.96; P<0.001 for noninferiority). In the intention-to-treat analysis, noninferiority was also met (hazard ratio, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.74 to 1.03; P<0.001 for noninferiority) but superiority was not shown (P = 0.12 for superiority). Major and nonmajor clinically relevant bleeding did not significantly differ (hazard ratio, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.96 to 1.11; P = 0.44), while intracranial hemorrhage (0.5% vs. 0.7% per year; P = 0.02) and fatal bleeding (0.2% vs. 0.5%; P = 0.003) were lower with rivaroxaban, and major gastrointestinal bleeding was more common with rivaroxaban (3.2% vs. 2.2%, P<0.001).

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, event-driven trial conducted at 1178 sites in 45 countries.
major_points.quote: The Rivaroxaban Once Daily Oral Direct Factor Xa Inhibition Compared with Vitamin K Antagonism for Prevention of Stroke and Embolism Trial in Atrial Fibrillation (ROCKET AF) was a multi- center, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, event-driven trial

major_points.text: Patients were randomly assigned to rivaroxaban 20 mg daily or dose-adjusted warfarin (target INR 2.0 to 3.0).
major_points.quote: we randomly assigned 14,264 patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation who were at increased risk for stroke to receive either rivaroxaban (at a daily dose of 20 mg) or dose-adjusted warfarin.

major_points.text: Primary efficacy end point was the composite of stroke (ischemic or hemorrhagic) and systemic embolism.
major_points.quote: The primary efficacy end point was the compos- ite of stroke (ischemic or hemorrhagic) and sys- temic embolism.

major_points.text: Primary analysis was per-protocol, as-treated, designed to test noninferiority for stroke or systemic embolism.
major_points.quote: The per-protocol, as-treated primary analysis was designed to determine whether rivaroxaban was noninferior to warfa- rin for the primary end point of stroke or systemic embolism.

major_points.text: Major and nonmajor clinically relevant bleeding rates were similar between groups, while intracranial hemorrhage and fatal bleeding were lower with rivaroxaban.
major_points.quote: Major and nonmajor clinically rel- evant bleeding occurred in 1475 patients in the rivaroxaban group (14.9% per year) and in 1449 in the warfarin group (14.5% per year)

absolute_effects.text: Per-protocol, as-treated: 188/6958 (1.7 no./100 patient-yr) vs 241/7004 (2.2 no./100 patient-yr); hazard ratio 0.79 (0.66–0.96); P<0.001.
Intention-to-treat: 269/7081 (2.1 no./100 patient-yr) vs 306/7090 (2.4 no./100 patient-yr); hazard ratio 0.88 (0.75–1.03); P<0.001 for noninferiority; P=0.12 for superiority.
Principal safety end point: 1475 (14.9 no./100 patient-yr) vs 1449 (14.5 no./100 patient-yr); hazard ratio 1.03 (0.96–1.11); P=0.44.

inclusion_criteria.text: Elevated risk indicated by history of stroke, transient ischemic attack, or systemic embolism, or at least two specified risk factors (CHADS2 score of 2 or more).

criticisms.text: Data from one site were excluded from all efficacy analyses due to Good Clinical Practice violations making the data unreliable.
criticisms.quote: Because of violations in Good Clinical Prac- tice guidelines at one site that made the data un- reliable, 93 patients (50 in the rivaroxaban group and 43 in the warfarin group) were excluded from all efficacy analyses before unblinding.

criticisms.text: Time in therapeutic range for warfarin was lower than in previous trials of other new anticoagulants in atrial fibrillation.
criticisms.quote: Among patients in the warfarin group, the pro- portion of time in which the intensity of anti- coagulation was in the therapeutic range (mean, 55%), which was calculated from all INR values during the study and for 7 days after warfarin interruptions, was lower than in previous studies
